english: The sum of all solutions of the equation
lying in the interval $[-\pi,0]$ is $\dfrac{k\pi}{6}$. Then the value of $k$ is ______.
hindi: के सभी हलों का योग $\dfrac{k\pi}{6}$ है। तब $k$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Sum-to-product: $\sin3x-\sin x=2\cos2x\sin x$ and $\cos3x+\cos x=2\cos2x\cos x$.
So the left side is $2\cos2x\left(\sin x+\sqrt3\cos x\right)$ and the equation becomes $2\cos2x\left(\sin x+\sqrt3\cos x-1\right)=0$.
Factor 2: $\sin x+\sqrt3\cos x=1$. Divide by $\sqrt{1^2+(\sqrt3)^2}=2$: $\frac12\sin x+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\cos x=\frac12$, i.e. $\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac12$.

For $x\in[-\pi,0]$, $x+\frac{\pi}{3}\in\left[-\frac{2\pi}{3},\frac{\pi}{3}\right]$. In this interval $\sin\theta=\frac12$ only at $\theta=\frac{\pi}{6}$ ($\frac{5\pi}{6}$ and $-\frac{7\pi}{6}$ lie outside). So $x=-\frac{\pi}{6}$.
Check: $\cos2\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac12\ne0$, so the three solutions are distinct.
originality_note: New: sum-to-product on two pairs produces the common factor cos 2x, leaving a sin x + sqrt3 cos x = 1 factor whose root must be located in [-pi, 0] by the shifted argument (way 5). Closest known: sin x + sin 3x = cos x + cos 3x type textbook items. Different because: the sqrt3 weighting makes the second factor an a sin + b cos = c equation, and only one of its roots lies in the interval.

concept_use.Solution by factorisation: Sum-to-product gives the factorised form 2 cos 2x (sin x + sqrt3 cos x - 1) = 0, and each factor is solved.
concept_use.Solution of a.sin(x) + b.cos(x) = c: sin x + sqrt3 cos x = 1 is written as sin(x + pi/3) = 1/2 and solved for x in [-pi, 0].

Closed interval: no solution sits at -pi or 0, so the sum is unambiguous. Changed: No change.
key_step: Applying sum-to-product to both pairs to extract the factor cos 2x.
justification: Routine chain: two sum-to-product formulas, one standard a sin + b cos = c reduction and an interval check; no insight beyond the grouping. Same demand as 2023-P1-Q8 (L2).
